reviews.text: Lack of communication and unsanitary rooms. The sink in our first room did not drain. It was our wedding night and no acknowledgment of that by the front desk.
reviews.author: jason steele

reviews.text:
Super disappointed to be writing this review as I have been wanting to stay at the Scott for years. This is also the first goodie review I have ever written, but given the marketing online I feel it important to review in order to help
people before they book! Service has been great and the lobby area so beautiful, but unfortunately that’s where the positives end.  Before you book beware!  The pool is completely filled with towels saving seats at 6:30 each morning of our stay. Because the pool area is smaller, people get up early to save seats. So, you are either forced to do the same or you will not have a spot at the pool. Everyone complained and the resort had someone removing towels and people eventually coming to what they thought was their saved seat only to find someone else there. Lots of altercations and yelling with other guests as a result.  Not the relaxing vibe you want during your vacation. We asked to see the manager and he apparently told his staff he was too busy to talk to us. Never heard of that before.  Also, the cleaning in the hallways and common areas leaves much to be desired. No vacuuming seen or heard in our hallway during the entire 5 nights of our stay.  Good online marketing but unfortunately  in person does not live up to it at all. Would stay somewhere else next time.
reviews.author: Jaime White

reviews.text: Rooms are clean and so comfortable with personality!
reviews.author: Christa Cooper

reviews.text:
Most overrated resort we’ve stayed at yet. Lipstick on a pig is the best explanation and the only reason the resort is getting two stars- very beautiful common areas and bedrooms- Instagram worthy and that is the only enjoyable aspect. Check-in was great and efficient- attendant very nice! Food was subpar- what you’d expect at a resort, and so not too much complaint about that.

On to the bad- our room was obviously not cleaned well- there was hair that could not be me or my husbands hair on the bathroom counter and on the nightstands and lamps. Our phone is broken and only works on speaker, found that out after trying to order room service and was hung up on 3 times. Guest services didn’t answer on multiple occasions after 15 rings- which made us late to our massage, which had a world of issues with it there, but that review was left on the spa’s page. Both our robes had stains on them. Room service menu had very little options.

And back to the good to finish the sandwich- wait staff at the pool were very attentive.

I know this sounds picky, but coming from Sedona and ending our honeymoon here I was very excited, and it just has not lived up to the Instagram bloggers realities... maybe they should focus on the paying guests and their experiences more?
reviews.author: Catherine White

reviews.text:
Great place to stay, even during Spring Break when WAY TOO FEW irresponsible college students were masks -- endangering all the hotel workers, staff, and visitors!  Geez!  I was an irresponsible college student ... But nothing like these kids!  Anyway, other than that -- it was an absolute delightful visit. A tad bit on the expensive side what with a $48 "resort" fee (but at least parking was free.)

Great staff, management, and most professional visitors (i.e., non-students) maintained social distance.

reviews.text:
My fourth time at the Scott resort. The service, accommodations, cleanliness have been disappointing. Not the same standard it used to be. The Wi-Fi was spotty when it worked at all, trash and wet towels left around the pool all night and not picked up in the morning for the new guests for the day. Coffee not available until 7 AM which for business travelers is a bit late.
Rooms quiet and well appointed.

reviews.text: I recently visited this location looking to discover something new for me. I had high hopes to eat at “The Canal Club” restaurant. But unfortunately, my stay was only a few minutes. My medical career wouldn’t allow me to see past the ignorance and recklessness of guests. Signs claiming to keep visitors and staff safe were quite frankly ignored. There were a group of people who actually said to me “I can’t believe people like you are still wearing a mask”, I have a wicked tongue, so I let them know exactly how I felt, but In a respectable and professional manner. reviews.text:
💄on a 🐖

No daily house keeping to refresh TP, towels, or empty trash. We had to leave it all in the hall.
No AC - 86° IN ROOM - the room has so hot the first night then we realized the AC was broke.  We called the front desk,  and instead of saying they'd send someone to fix it or look at it,  they said,  "oh, is the room not cool enough for you?" No,  86 degrees is not cool enough. Someone did eventually come and fix it, so that was good.
No phone in room to easily call the front desk.
Out of the 7 times we called the front desk,  they answered twice. Decided to text the number we were given to "request anything from front desk" to reserve the gym for the next day, get to the gym to find out they didn't make our reservation, so we had to go off site and pay to use another gym.
Asked for facial and hand towels twice for room, only brought large towels.
Breakfast was not open at 7:45am on a Saturday.
The coffee was the same price, large or small, they let me buy a small and didn't tell me - coffee was good though. Then the next day I was told they only have one size of coffee and it was a small.
Paid $300 for shaded cabana, waste of money given most of the pool was in the shade anyway. The second day when we were not in a cabana, the waitress kept coming to the people next to us, but not to us.  When we finally got her attention, she said, "you guys are good, right?" Then when we said no and that we'd like to order drinks, she treated us like we were an inconvenience.
There are creepy paintings of people's faces all over the hotel and in rooms/ bathrooms. The rooms smell like an old motel 8 - musty/smoke.
The spa is over priced.  Friend got a massage and an "eye treatment." She paid $25 for little patches you can get at any retail store for $2. Definitely was not a "treatment."
We were on the second floor and there was no elevator and we were there for 3 nights, making it difficult to get our large bags to the room and we had someone with knee issues in our group.  It was manageable, but not pleasant or preferred.
Checked out early, paid extra for a late checkout,  was not refunded (as of now). The resort fee was ridiculous given there were no amenities I would expect a resort would offer... told there was no shuttle,  but they knew a guy with a golf cart that could take us places, and just check in with thy front desk to schedule. So we came back later and asked for the golf cart guy but they couldn't get ahold of him so they told us to Uber or walk.
I would not stay here again.  With all the issues we had I do have to say the hotel was cute and trendy, somewhat clean,  and the food and drinks were good, but over priced.  Most of the staff was friendly, with the exception of the pool waitress and the front desk was hit and miss. Was a bit disappointed with it being a "spa" resort and the amenities in the room were lacking severally. Seems like there could have been a liquid hand soap like in the common area bathrooms, but there was only the giant bottle of lotion.  There was one bar soap and one facial soap to share for both bathroom and shower. The fridge didn't get very cold and it stocked full of stuff that we didn't want so we had to empty and put everything in the closet so we could use it for our stuff,  then move it all back before we checked out so we didn't get charged for it.  I was also disappointed they didn't offer us a ground level floor, or even ask if the second level would work for us.  They just said, "I have you on the second floor and there is no elevator."  I did appreciate the very very small discount ($120 pool charge), that was taken off our total bill($1800) upon checkout, but regardless, I will not return or recommend this place to friends or family.

reviews.text:
The resort design is by far one of the best I've seen. Every detail counts. Every room is beautiful in every angle (besides the fact our balcony looked to the parking lot while the resort was not in full capacity ). It is definitely worth the millions invested in the design - both interior and graphic. Service was great as well.
However, and it's a big one, we were looking forward to a relaxing day at the pool (after a long week), and it was quite the opposite. At 930am, we managed to find almost the last available beds. The server told us it's due to COVID-19, which made sense, BUT apparently, the hotel is selling a day-pass to the pool! Around 11 am, the pool started to get very busy; 2 of the cabanas had a party of 10 people each. There were no available beds, so people began sitting on the edge of the pool. By 2 pm, there was no single spot around the pool and inside! They have two pools! It seemed like there is no cap on the number of people getting in; it felt like a pool party more than a resort. People even brought their own speakers playing their music (I counted 3). It was so disappointing, not to mention that during COVID-19, there wasn't any 6feet you can keep apart unless you stay on your bed (which added a nice anxiety effect to it). I reached out to the server about it, and she told me she forward my concern to the manager and front desk, yet no one came to resolve it. You would be happy to hear that there is no cleaning service either (CDC rules) and if you want something replaced or from the minibar, you need to call and ask for it.

reviews.text:
Let’s start of with the positives:
1. Every single employee I encountered here was super upbeat, extremely friendly, and very accommodating. There is no doubt management does a great job training everyone to have great customer service.
2. The vibes in the lobby, pool area and courtyard area are very relaxing and trendy. Very beautiful resort. Also, the smell of the hallways and lobby is awesome. Turns out they have a custom smell. Love!!
3. The drinks and food. Drinks are well made and the food is what you would expect at a higher-end resort.
Unfortunately, we have quite a bit of cons:
1. Poor communication. I originally had planned our stay July 9-12, as the resort was opening back up on the 7th. I received an email my reservation would be cancelled (no phone call nor refund posted to my account) due to the reopening date being pushed to the 10th. After contacting the hotel and not having lodging in the area needed, we decided it would be best to push the trip to a different weekend. This worked as the room rates were cheaper, however, they wouldn’t refund the difference to my bank as I was rescheduling the dates. Not cool. After a few days of waiting for the manager to contact me back regarding receiving a refund vs a credit, I decided to go the positive route and upgrade to a Parlor Suite, thus using the credit while increasing the total rate.
2. Inside the rooms. The refrigerators are not cold enough for health food safety, and you’re not able to adjust the temperature. Unfortunately, the food we tried to save for my daughter went rancid, as well as our probiotics ($50 wasted).
The photos of the suites are deceiving. Great marketing on their part, but we were all a little disappointed when walking in. Make sure to check out the photos off the website to get a better idea of what they look like.
Make sure to bring your own water if you’re not interested in paying $5-$8/bottle of water. Disappointed they didn’t provide complementary water to drink in the rooms.
3. The air conditioning unit. It would loudly bang each time it turned off (about every 45 mins) in the room with the Murphy bed. The second night of our stay I thought my daughter had fallen out of the bed and I ran into the room (twice) to see what was going on. The last night of our stay we chose to sleep without the ac, and when it’s hot outside and you don’t have ac, sleeping is miserable. Why didn’t we switch rooms you ask? Because we had to switch rooms after our first night because there was a HUGE Pala Verde Beatle in the bathroom on the toilet paper roll (see photo), and we didn’t feel it was worth switching rooms yet again.

Final mentions - I am waiting for the manager to contact me back via phone regarding the ac issue as I flew back this morning. I mentioned this on the phone to the front desk, but I received a text to receive a complementary facial at their spa. Hard to cash in when I’m already in a different state. Considering we had more than 1 person stay in a room that had a faulty ac unit, I hope they can accommodate more than one free facial that we cannot use. I’ll update this posting once I hear back. Frankly, I’m exhausted at this point as it’s been a bit of an uphill battle.

reviews.text: Horrible experience here.  My wife and I got a rare weekend without the kids, so we scheduled a stay here since it looks so fantastic in the pictures.  They were marketing "grand reopening" deals after their "completed" renovations to the pools and resort.  I called on 7/7/2020, before making the reservation, to confirm the the work was on schedule and the pools and rooms would truly be complete for the 7/10/2020 grand reopening.  I was reassured that everything was on schedule and would be open on 7/10/2020 for our arrival.  I called again on 7/10/2020, before driving to the resort, to confirm again, and I was again reassured that everything complete and ready for our stay.  A few hours later we arrived to find a frantic resort staff, 1 pool drained, the other pool still getting filled while the new decking tile was being sealed, as the staff ran about trying to place furniture and umbrellas while guest waited.  We then talked to the front desk who informed us that the king bed rooms, as we had booked, were not finished and therefore not available for the weekend.  They offered us a double queen bed room, which isn't what we wanted for our weekend without the kids, or 1/2 of a suite room with a murphy bed, which looked nice, but was not at all what we wanted, nor did we want 1/2 of a nice room with someone else staying on the other side of the closed door that separated the rooms.  The staff apologized many times, and were very polite as they tried to cater to the many disappointed guests, but we ended up having to cancel our reservation and go to another resort.  In all, this was a very disappointing first experience.  It'd take a lot for me to give them a second chance after being lied to several times as I attempted to avoid the exact experience that we ended up stuck in...

reviews.text:
The stay started off great until we fell asleep and woke up to a hot room. Called the front desk and they tried finding a room that was cooler but every single available room didn’t have working ac. The guy that helped us was apologetic and said that they ac units haven’t been serviced in months and this has been an ongoing problem for years.

The fact that the hotel operators have known this was a problem for years and haven’t replaced the ac units is crazy. Especially since they have just finished a renovation which they replaced the pool and a bunch of other things. Would have been nice if they had spent some extra money and replaced the ac units. This is Arizona, ac units are a priority

Everything about this resort was just top notch.
When we walked into the lobby oy was beautiful. They treated us like we were the only guests there. The royalty treatment carried over to our room, it was absolutely beautiful.
We spent time at the pool and I enjoyed ordering food at the pool. Every member of their staff was amazing. It didn't matter if we were by ourself of by 20 other people they made everyone feel like they were the most important guest.
We had a small problem with the A/C in our room. They moved mountains trying to help us. They offered to change our room (I declined, I didn't want to move our luggage). They brought us fans and did everything to make it better.
I can't say enough good things about the service at this resort.
I also LOVED the text feature. You could text for anything you needed. Front desk, towels anything. It was a great feature.
This will definitely be our resort of choice in Scottsdale and we will recommend to our family and friends.

reviews.text:
When I came to Scottsdale & chose the Scott, a good deal of it was due to the fact that it had been newly refurbished (it is beautiful) & for its close proximity to Old Town Scottsdale. And it is walking distance but the resort also has shuttles on demand up until 11:30 p.m. that will take you up to 5 Miles.

I really wanted to be somewhere where I could get a good deal of relaxation and Spa use and treatments.  However I was VERY DISAPPOINTED on this level. I would never call this place a spa. I've stayed at a lot of spas. This spa is extremely small and does not have many amenities other than treatment rooms. There are no soaking tubs, steam room, sauna, quiet room or other things you might expect in a spa. As I said you pay for treatments and they are far from inexpensive. For example a manicure was $50.  So if you're going for a spa experience, look elsewhere.

The pools are nice but again they are mere wading pools. They are not pools that you can swim in. This was another huge disappointment for me because I am a swimmer. Also it was not monitored very well. Children have their own pool and many of them were in the adult pool throwing balls around and splashing. I don't mean to sound like a crab, but if you have a dedicated pool for children that's where they should be.  also drink service is available at the pool but my friends and I waited an hour for our cocktails to be delivered. When it was time for another round we just went inside to the bar itself.

The rooms are very attractive. And the beds are firm & comfortable. The place is kept very clean and that is always important.  The bathrooms are incredibly small and the toilet paper is like sandpaper. You might want to bring your own. The grounds are also very well kept and attractive to look at. I also enjoyed the fact that we had a balcony. Most of the rooms have balconies or patios.

Found the service to be uniformly excellent. The Valets & drivers were particularly helpful in providing tips of places to see and eat.
reviews.author: Karen Heckler

reviews.text:
The decor of this hotel is beautiful, the room was nice, but that's where it ends.  I unfortunately have more cons than pros to share.  The cons being that they have 2 pools, but not enough room or chairs. My husband and I got in around 1pm on a Friday and there was no room at the pool.  However we understood that it was a Friday and later in the day so no biggie.  The next day we got to the pool bright and early, 9:30am and there was still no spots.  People had put towels on all the chairs to "save" them.  I saw chairs sitting there for over 3 hours with towels and no people.
On Friday night we went to the hotel bar for their happy hour.  There were minimal people at the bar, but it took over 15 minutes to even be acknowledged by a bartender and I'm the one who had to acknowledge him and ask if I could order a drink.  Then the drinks took over 15 minutes to make...and my husband had a whiskey on the rocks, nothing too time consuming to put together.
Last, I would say that this is not a resort for couples.  I don't necessarily thinks that's a "con"  but something that should be made clear.  The women outnumber the males 3 to 1 as the resort was packed with groups of ladies celebrating 30th birthdays, 40th birthdays, bachelorette parties.

reviews.text:
It’s awesome to go to a “resort” that charges a $50 a day resort fee on top of the room that sells pool passes to people not staying there. There are no lounge chairs and people laying on the  concrete on towels all around the pool. Yesterday there was trash all around the pool and the staff was not cleaning it up. I absolutely would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

Additionally the restaurant is just okay, the management is questionable at best and the service was unremarkable. Do yourself a favor, spend the same amount of money and go to a nice resort in Mexico or Costa Rica where they are still proving that they actually want your money. Or anything else in Scottsdale (Arizona as a whole has been amazing, this hotel is just garbage).

My husband also tried calling the spa a week in advance while I was pregnant so I could get a massage on our anniversary but no one would call him back to set up and appointment while we were staying. So we thought we could walk over and see if they had anything available. They didn't, the best they could do was after the weekend. Which was when we were leaving. They informed us to make an appointment. We just said ok. Was super frustrating. Then we had to to go to an overcrowded pool and I had to sit on the side of the pool. I also notice walking around the resort inside and out when passing staff Or any of the young ladies up at the concierge wasn't really that friendly and didn't have smiles on their faces which seemed to be a little disturbing We passed a few different and please out on the grounds around the grounds and none of them was saying  Hi can I help you or can i get you anything.... nothing from the staff to me or my family... We bought a day pass and loved the resort/pools. Unfortunately, we experienced a lot of inconvenience from a sewer issue. It took from about 11am till around 7:30pm, and within that time frame (in other words, the whole day) we couldn't use the restrooms, nor eat anything, there was no running water. The restrooms were full of pee and poop and not being able to use the restrooms with kids really is a problem. They were working on the sewer system the whole day, which took place next to the pool area/day beds, and it was very unpleasant.
On top of that, there was also a problem with the a/c, which did not work anywhere inside. This all took away our otherwise great experience with The Scott, we would have loved it otherwise. During check-out that evening, nobody apologized for the inconvenience. Because we were there for only that day, we feel that some sort of refund would have been appropriate.

The staff was very accommodating and pleasant, the music was fabulous outside near the pool and in the lounging area. The food service was above average but not amazing. I would highly recommend this location anybody who loves the Bohemian, Jamaican, Beachy theme feel! As you can tell I took tons of interior pictures of the resort. reviews.text: Très belle hôtel à Scottdale, au cœur des quartiers chics et des centres commerciaux de qualités. L’ensemble du lobby a été refait à l’été 2017 avec son nouveau style Caribéens. Le plus gros des chambres a été entièrement rénovées, elles sont immenses et parfaitement équipées. La ligne de décoration oscillant entre Cuba et La Havane a permis au décorateur comme au propriétaire de nous proposer une ambiance thématique et cohérente sur l’ensemble des locaux de ce grand et convivial hôtel. Le personnel est très professionnel. La végétation est luxuriante. La troisième piscine qui sera terminée dernier trimestre 2018 offrira un espace extérieur encore plus grand. En résumé un grand et bel hôtel où il fait bon séjourner quelques nuits ou plus.

reviews.text:
Spent 1 night here on July 1. Arrived at 4pm to a TRASHED pool area. I counted over 40 towels all over the place. Empty drink cups in the bushes, by the pool, stashed everywhere. A gentleman came out at 8PM and began cleaning the area. Needlesd to say, we were VERY disappointed. We did not even use the pool which was the main reason why we booked the resort. We sat by the pool but, once we realized their was a couple in the hot tub obviously having sexual relations, we left the area.
Not once during our stay did one member of your management team ever greet us, after sitting in your lobby for three hours on Monday morning. The had all gathered in the lobby for their morning meeting and did not make eye contact with one guest. As a Director of Sales at a 4 star resort in the Valley, bringing a guest here because I was told that your property had a cool "Cuban vibe" was very diisapointing. I did not attach any photos so, you obviously confused my review with someone else's. As a previous Reservations Manager at a 5 Star Caribbean resort, I'd suggest more customer service training for your restaurant staff.

reviews.text: So first of all the place is awesome! So beautiful and relaxing and peaceful. The ambiance is great, the bartender right inside of the pool was great! My boyfriend took me here as a surprise for my birthday. The first hotel was not what we expected at The Claredon but had an amazing staff that replaced and made up for EVERYTHING in this "older style" hotel. Tried round two at The Scott and had the reverse effects. Very nice hotel, unfortunately a horrible, rude, disrepectful security staff. We were packing our room which happened to be on the first floor with our truck parked directly on the other side. We put the bags up on the wall, (mind you, my boyfriend has a broken tibia and fibula and it was only him and I) and we locked up the door and were finished. The amount of time it took to get all the bags on the wall and throw some trash out, we were approached and awkwardly stared at as we walked toward the parking lot. Apparently our actions (Bags on wall)  were "unsuitable" and not a "good look" for their hotel. Saddest thing was how extremely disrespected and degrading we felt. A woman manager was notified when we checked out the day of tuesday june 5th. She had said the male employee has been with the company for quite some time and that she felt the bags on the wall were not okay (in her own words). NO disappointed tone of voice, NO apologetic nature in her facial expression or response. I assume as a manager whether you want to fake the apology or not, at least show some sign of repect that we were guests that had paid for two nights and we felt extremely unwelcomed as we were on our way out. I was in absolute awe with the managers response to my bf and I.

reviews.text:
I’m currently staying at the Scott and overall have been very impressed. The hotel grounds and common areas are beautiful, with lots of attention to landscaping.

Our room, whilst I think is classified as ‘renovated’, many smaller details like fixtures and fittings - most noticeably the shower head - could do with updating. And I’m not sure why there was just one robe in the cupboard and no slippers.

I was intending to rate the property a 4, but during the last two days of using the pool I have become really disappointed by the lack of management when it comes to maintaining a relaxing and considerate environment.  Both days different guests have found nothing wrong with playing their own personal music out loud (despite the fact there is low-volume background music already playing by the pool).  What kind of person does that? It’s not spring break, but a family resort. I wish the management would do something about this; the place is supposed to be a relaxing spa resort.

Lastly, the wi-if option included in the room rate is virtually unusable.

reviews.text:
The FireSky is motel-style resort in Scottsdale, AZ that's part of the Kimpton chain. (2016 Update: No longer a Kimpton Hotel) We've stayed at several Kimpton hotels before and loved them, so expectations were high for our 4 nights here.

Overall, we are very impressed with the FireSky. Although it's obvious that it started life in the 50's or 60's as a motel, Kimpton has done a nice job renovating and restoring it up to the chain's standards. Rooms are outfitted nicely and everything is no more than a 2 minute walk to the pool and lobby area. There's a few places where the resort is showing its age, but overall the decor is excellent and the rooms was very clean. Wi-Fi was very good.

Speaking of the pool, it's fantastic. 2 pools actually, 1 for kids with a small beach area, and a larger one lined with loungers and cabanas. There's a pool bar as well with cocktails, etc, and they take orders for snacks and lunch. At night, the whole area becomes beautifully illuminated with fiery torches, pool lights and cascading LED's in the trees. So gorgeous, you'll think you're in Hawaii!

The staff were very friendly and professional. And the spacious lobby is a happening place, with coffee in the morning and an evening wine reception each night at 5:30.

Very satisfied with our stay at the FireSky!

reviews.text:
I haven't decided if I will keep my reservation - so technically I haven't stayed yet.  I would like to share my booking experience... booked online.
In website under "free" amenities... it lists Free WiFi, Free Parking, Pool, Hot Tub, Gym... few others.   When I saw the hotel final price there was $166 increase - at first I assumed taxes but then I did a little math and this was 25% of base room rate.  So I called & asked what's in taxes & fees ...person responded there is a $22/nite "resort" fee.  I then asked what's in the resort fee... she said  WiFi, Parking, Pool, Gym..  I say I don't have a car why am I paying for valet parking and the other items are listed as free.

Response..it's a mandatory fee.   I find this very deceiving.  If hotel wants to charge a higher rate then do so but saying things are free and charging anyway using a different name convention is a joke and poor business.

reviews.text: My husband and I had an overall great experience staying at FireSky.  To start, the concierge was outstanding.  Offering rides within a few miles from the hotel, we didn't have to deal with waiting for taxis.  On they days we wanted to venture out, they gave recommendations of where to go out for lunch/diner, and where to hike and bike.  Being from the flat lands, Camelback was an awesome hiking experience.  We stayed in a clean, spacious 2nd floor room with a pool view, highly recommended.  We were a little worried as to if we would have a good time by the pools with it being the beginning of September, and in the high 90s.  The pool was kept cool, and their were plenty of chairs to sit in the shade or sun.   If any of my friends or family ask me where to stay in AZ, this is the spot.

reviews.text:
This was probably the worst Hotel, I have ever had.  When we initial got there at noon our room wasn't ready which is understandable concentering that check in is 4:00pm. So we then decided to hang out at the pool, but there were no pool towels available so we scratched that.  We went to the bar to have lunch and we meet Will the bartender, who was very pleasant and had lunch. After lunch we walked around, and that's when I noticed the pool view on the first floor like we requested was starring at the pool gate. So I went to the front desk and asked if there was something on the 2nd floor but there really wasn't anything available, so I asked if we could just get the Lagoon view instead even though was still charged for pool view.  The lady at the front desk did try to accommodate our group and but us together.

Here is when it gets fun, we asked the restaurant if they can accommodate 10ppl as we were celebrating two birthday parties.  They got us set up pretty much in the middle of the restaurant. Our server came and got our drink and appetizer order, told us about the specials.  We were talked and joking around like a normal group of 10 would. That's when our waiter came and told us we need to be QUIET we are way too loud, it was bothering other guests.  At this point we had probably only been in the restaurant for about 30 minutes and have a group of 10ppl, how can you ask ten people to stop talking. I didn't realize that we were in a library and not a restaurant. We have been to restaurants all over the valley including 5 stars restaurants and resorts and never ever had someone basically tell us to shut up. Everyone at the table was very offended so we all got up and left, went to another restaurant in Old Town Scottsdale that was more than Happy to take our group and enjoyed having us.

This experience could have been handled in a more professional matter instead of the way it was.  That just shows us the lack of experience the staff has.
reviews.author: Eiva Paulis

reviews.text:
The FireSky Resort, is our home away from home during MLB Spring Training. We (Rick and I) come out every March and love staying at this resort.  We have been staying there, me for the last 4 years, and for Rick -- ever since the resort was The Sunburst!  The Firesky property is beautiful, relaxing and very welcoming...a tropical paradise in the desert.  The fire pit areas are a great place to hang out at night with a bottle or 2 or 3 of wine and good friends (and to meet new ones).   For pet-owners, the property is pet-friendly!!  The Resort’s staff is friendly, helpful, professional and respectful….and, it seems, with little to zero personnel turnaround.  We are greeted by the same staff year-after-year.  Speaking of the staff……

Valet Staff, in particular, Mike, Brian and Jeremy.  They’ve been greeting us, at least for the last 4 years.  It's always great to see them upon our arrival. We know our vacation has really started when we see them!  Thanks guys for (1) taking care of our transportation needs, and (2) providing restaurant recommendations and for making reservations too!   Their recommendations have been RIGHT ON!  AND, these guys will even provide a ride to the pharmacy/supermarket (and wait for you)!!   A special "thank you" to Mike for the special arrangement in getting us to Hohokum Stadium during our recent visit....we owe you!

Front Desk/Reservation staff is quite accommodating.  (Gail) you rock lady and you're funny too!  Thanks for always working with Rick on our reservations and getting us the room(s) that Rick ask for year after year (except for that gliche last year).  Glad we finally met you this past visit.

Bartenders are friendly, especially Benny!   He’s like family.  Benny is always there when we come to visit.  A greeting from Benny makes you feel like you’ve come home.   However, we missed Benny during our recent visit.  It's the first time we didn't see Benny during any of our stay at the resort.  We were sad when we didn't see him as we approached, what we consider, “Benny’s Bar”.  Just wasn’t the same.  But, we do have to thank the other bartenders for keeping us hydrated ;-)   "Thanks"  you guys/gals are great, too.

The guest rooms are clean and comfortable, but we do feel that it's time for some updating to be done.  Making them a little brighter and updating some of the furnishing would be nice.  Overall, we always enjoy our time at the Firesky and plan on returning again and again.  See you next March, if not sooner!

Annette & Rick (and Tom, too)

reviews.text:
The first thing guests absolutely have to be aware of is that when booking through a third party (e.g. Hotwire, Priceline) you've already paid ALL the taxes and fees, INCLUDING the resort fee.

When we checked out, the front desk attendant charged us $104 for the resort fee plus taxes on the resort fee (roughly $22/day) He didn't tell us that he was about to charge our card for that amount, he just did it. When I informed him that I had already paid for the resort fee when I booked through Priceline, and that I had confirmed that I paid my fees by calling FireSky right after I booked, he didn't believe me and asked that I show him proof. Fortunately, I still had my confirmation email from Priceline that included a line item for fees and taxes. Acting rather petulantly, he refunded my credit card but offered no apology for a blatant overcharge.

How many people end up double paying the resort fee because they didn't realize that they already paid it? It's obviously highly improbable that we were the first ones double charged. This is completely unacceptable, and the front desk attendant's peevish, almost cavalier attitude, like WE did something wrong, was disconcerting.

The pool at this resort is beautiful, and really the best thing it has going for it. However, they have a rule that you cannot use the pool or the hot tub after midnight. When I called to ask why, I was told by a VERY irritated front desk attendant that "rules are rules." No clear explanation was given.

There is only one restaurant at this resort and the service is very average. The food is ok.

The bartenders were friendly.

The location is great, minutes from downtown Scottsdale.

Overall, I was not impressed with the level of service, and especially dismayed by being double charged for a resort fee.
reviews.author: Eugene Slaven

reviews.text: My husband and I recently celebrated our 20th wedding anniversary at the FireSky Resort and had an amazing time.  We were upgraded to a room with patio opening to what are beautiful grounds and were thrilled to find in our room, upon arrival, a bottle of champagne - compliments of the staff (thank you!).  The location is perfect.  We enjoyed several runs to and over Camelback Mountain (roundtrip... about 8 miles for those of you who love to run) along with a more relaxing run along the canal.  We took advantage of their shuttle service and had dinner nearby at The Mission and Citizen Public House.  We also dined in one evening at Taggia (I recommend the scallops and Tiramisu).  Our waitress was exceptional - personable and funny.  The pool area is very pretty (although we did struggle to find a little patch of sun as there are many trees - perfect setting for the hot weather).  Hope to visit again!

reviews.text: We had an awesome 5-day Girls Getaway at Firesky recently!  Our entire experience from check-in to check-out was superb.  The resort is welcoming, clean, and so very relaxing.  Jen H and Alex at the front desk were both so patient, friendly and helpful. We loved the nightly hosted wine hour and enjoyed the friendly atmosphere in the "living room" as well as the live music on the weekend. The covered patios off the well decorated rooms, were cool and relaxing.  We want to specifically mention Firesky's amazing poolside ambassador, Sarah. Sarah was so fun, friendly and engaged with each of the guests.  It is very obvious that she truly cares about the guests and was interested in not only our experience at the resort, but also in who we are back home in the "real world".  She never missed a smile, wave, or fun story while we enjoyed the sun at the pool.  You have a gem there, Firesky. She is an awesome young lady with an obvious bright future and will forever be a huge part of our fabulous vacation memories!

reviews.text: Hotels in Scottsdale AZ are everywhere. Best Hotel in Scottsdale AZ is only one. Fire Sky Resort is the best in Comfort, Guest Service, Customer Service, Food, Bar, and Front Desk. Upon entering the hotel doorman greet's you with a friendly smile. But wait. When you enter the hotel the front desk is located just inside. You will be shocked at the two young ladys who will check you in. The most friendly smile's and bubbleing over with joy,(Alex and Jessica) will have you smiling and laughing and just plain make you happy you picked the best of the best in hotels. Service comes first in this hotel and that is what we are all looking for. Beautiful Pool area that is perfect at night with such a wonderful view. Kristen at the bar makes you feel at home. Never had such a perfect bartender as this. Wish I could import this hotel to my home location. Alex, Jessica and Kristen get 5 Stars. *****

reviews.text:
3/17-19/2013: Horrendous food poisoning from lettuce in FireSky restaurant. Violently sick on 2nd night of what was to be a get-a-way to Scottsdale, Az. with my sister. So sick I could not get out of the bathroom for over 36 hours. Consequently, I was stranded in room for a third night. The hotel manager awarded me with a sudden phone call to my room informing me he was charging me a $435.00 Plus bill for the third night instead of the $128.00 I was paying for each if the planned 2 nights. Wonderful caring and compassionate management in action while throwing up during the phone call to me. As an aside, the TV was broken in the room, there were no toiletries after first night (original only tiny tube of shampoo and conditioner for ONE person not two). Frankly, this manager, and Michael A. Depatie, CEO of Kimpton hotel chain should pay me for their "treat" of violent food poisoning, broken TV, and lack of supplies. Instead, Mr. Depatie can add the 4 times more of a one night charge to me to his pocket in the name of good management. Kimpton should be removed from Scottsdale, Arizona or, at least, fined by the City of Scottsdale for their indignant arrogant manners and pitiful service. For that price, I would have gotten a suite with all the gratuities and trimmings at the Tucson airport for only a fraction of what Kimpton pockets in Scottsdale. Shame of Scottsdale, Arizona, for housing such a rotten group of gentlemen managers. This is Capitalism at its finest in action in our good ole USA. People will do better in a roadside motel anywhere in the U.S. Scottsdale is a mean place to visit!!!!

P.S. After much complaining, on check-out, the resort knocked off a hundred bucks so I could share in the hotel's loss. Still a bill over $300.00 for the lovely sick night and food poisoning courtesy of FireSky Resort & Spa in Scottsdale.
